title: How The U.S. Doomsday Plane Works
fullText: A nuclear war has just begun. Washington has been attacked. The Pentagon is gone. Military bases have been destroyed. Communications are failing. And the country's normal command structure has been wiped out. But somewhere thousands of feet above the United States, a Boeing 747 is still flying. Inside it, military officers are working at computer terminals, communicating with forces around the world, and preparing to keep America's nuclear arsenal under control. This is the E4B, better known as the American Doomsday plane. And despite looking like an ordinary Boeing 747 from the outside, it is one of the most unusual aircraft ever built. Because its job isn't to win a war, its job is to make sure the United States can still fight one after everything else has been destroyed. Welcome to Simple Concepts Explained. Today, we're pulling back the curtain on the US doomsday plane, how it can survive a nuclear attack, how it communicates with submarines hiding beneath the ocean, and why the United States keeps a flying command center ready for the worst day imaginable. To understand why the E4B exists, we need to go back to the Cold War. During the 1950s and 1960s, the United States and Soviet Union built enormous nuclear arsenals, each capable of destroying the other. America's nuclear forces were controlled through a complex command structure. At the very top was the president. If the president ordered a nuclear strike, that order would pass through military command centers before reaching the forces responsible for carrying it out. One of the most important locations was strategic air command at Offet Air Force Base in Nebraska. The system worked, provided those command centers were still functioning. And that created a terrifying weakness. What happens if the United States is attacked first? A nuclear explosion can produce an electromagnetic pulse capable of damaging electrical infrastructure and vulnerable electronics. At the same time, an enemy would presumably target the country's most important military and political centers. The White House could be destroyed. The Pentagon could be destroyed. Off could be destroyed. Even the communications networks connecting them could disappear. America could still have nuclear weapons, but the people responsible for commanding them might no longer have any way of communicating with them. And during the Cold War, that wasn't just a theoretical problem. The entire concept of nuclear deterrence depended on one thing. If you destroy America, America can still retaliate. This became part of the logic behind mutually assured destruction. So, the United States developed a backup command system that couldn't simply be destroyed on the ground. it would fly. This became known as Operation Looking Glass. Beginning in 1961, specially modified aircraft were kept airborne around the clock. At least one aircraft was always flying, day and night, ready to take over nuclear command if the groundbased command structure was destroyed. And incredibly, this continuous airborne alert lasted for 29 years. From 1961 until 1990, there was always an American aircraft in the sky, ready for the worstc case scenario. Eventually, the older EC135 aircraft were replaced by specially modified Boeing 747s. These became the E4B fleet, and today there are just four of them. From the outside, the E4B looks like a Boeing 747. Inside, however, it is essentially a flying military command center. At the front of the aircraft is a command area and VIP suite. This is where senior leadership can work with the Secretary of Defense being one of the people who may use the aircraft during normal operations. Behind this is a galley and a small conference room. But this isn't just somewhere for senior officials to have a meeting. In a national emergency, this could effectively become a flying situation room where decisions affecting the entire country are made. Further back is a briefing area. There are phones and communication equipment designed to keep the aircraft connected to military units, government agencies, and command centers around the world. And then comes one of the most important sections of the aircraft, the battle staff area. This is essentially a flying office filled with workstations. Military personnel can monitor events, communicate with other forces, and coordinate America's response to a national emergency. But none of this would be useful without communications. And that is where the E4B becomes truly unusual. The aircraft contains multiple redundant communication systems. If one network fails, operators can switch to another. The aircraft also has a specialized satellite communication system housed inside the distinctive hump on top of the 747. This provides a secure link to military satellites orbiting above the Earth. But the most unusual system is hidden inside the aircraft because sometimes satellites aren't enough. The E4B carries a massive spool of antenna cable that can be deployed while the aircraft is flying. The cable trails behind the aircraft and can extend for around 5 m. Why would anyone need an antenna that long? Because the aircraft needs to communicate using extremely low frequency radio waves. These wavelengths are enormous, meaning an effective antenna also needs to be extremely large. And there's another reason these frequencies are so important. They can partially penetrate seawater. That means the E4B can communicate with one of the most important parts of America's nuclear arsenal, ballistic missile submarines. These submarines can hide beneath the ocean for long periods, making them incredibly difficult to locate and destroy. But that also creates a communication problem. If the United States needs to send an order to a submarine underwater, normal radio systems aren't going to work particularly well. The E4B's trailing antenna provides a way to reach them. The aircraft even has operators dedicated to managing the system. They monitor the cable through a small viewing system and communicate with the pilots to make sure the aircraft maintains the correct speed and altitude. The aircraft itself is also designed for endurance. The E4B can be refueled while airborne, meaning it doesn't necessarily need to land when fuel runs low. Under extreme circumstances, the aircraft is designed to remain airborne for days at a time. The original source describes a theoretical endurance of around a week. That means the aircraft could remain in the sky while the situation on the ground changes completely. And there's another major difference between the E4B and an ordinary Boeing 747. The aircraft has been hardened against the effects of a nuclear attack. Many of its systems are designed to withstand the electromagnetic effects of a nuclear detonation. The windows contain wire mesh designed to help protect sensitive electronics from electromagnetic pulses. And despite operating in an age of sophisticated digital avionics, many of the aircraft's controls remain analog. That's because in this particular aircraft, older technology can actually be safer. The objective isn't to have the most advanced aircraft possible. It's to have an aircraft that still works when everything around it doesn't. And the E4B isn't working alone. The United States also operates E6 Mercury aircraft through the Navy. These have overlapping nuclear command and communications responsibilities and form another layer of redundancy. And redundancy is really the entire point of this system. America doesn't simply have one command center. It has multiple command centers. It doesn't have one communication system. It has multiple communication systems. And it doesn't rely entirely on aircraft sitting safely on the ground. It has aircraft capable of taking those functions into the sky. Because the entire system is designed around one terrifying assumption. What if everything else fails? The E4B isn't designed to fly into a nuclear blast and simply emerge untouched. Instead, it is designed around something much more important. Survival of command. The United States's nuclear arsenal only acts as a deterrent if an enemy believes America can respond to an attack. Destroying Washington shouldn't mean destroying the country's ability to retaliate. Destroying communication networks shouldn't mean losing contact with submarines. And destroying military command centers shouldn't mean there is nobody left to make decisions. That's what the doomsday plane is ultimately designed to prevent. It turns one of the most vulnerable parts of nuclear warfare, the command structure, into something that can move. A command center that can't be easily targeted because it is thousands of feet in the air. A communication system that can use satellites, radio networks, and even a 5m long trailing antenna. And a military headquarters that can remain airborne for days if necessary. It's an aircraft built around a concept that sounds almost contradictory. The less likely you think nuclear war is, the more useful the doomsday plane becomes because its existence is intended to make nuclear war less likely in the first place. An enemy needs to believe that even a devastating first strike won't eliminate America's ability to respond. And as long as that belief exists, the doomsday plane doesn't need to do what it was built for. It simply needs to be ready. Thanks for watching Simple Concepts Explained. segments.viText: Đó là bởi vì trên chiếc máy bay đặc biệt này, công nghệ cũ thực sự có thể an toàn hơn.

segments.text: The objective isn't to have the most advanced aircraft possible.
segments.viText: Mục tiêu không phải là có được chiếc máy bay tiên tiến nhất có thể.

segments.text: It's to have an aircraft that still works when everything around it doesn't.
segments.viText: Đó là có một chiếc máy bay vẫn hoạt động được khi mọi thứ xung quanh nó không hoạt động.

segments.text: And the E4B isn't working alone.
segments.viText: Và E4B không hoạt động một mình.

segments.text: The United States also operates E6 Mercury aircraft through the Navy.
segments.viText: Hoa Kỳ cũng vận hành máy bay E6 Mercury thông qua Hải quân.

segments.text: These have overlapping nuclear command and communications responsibilities and form another layer of redundancy.
segments.viText: Những cơ quan này có trách nhiệm chỉ huy và liên lạc hạt nhân chồng chéo và tạo thành một lớp dự phòng khác.

segments.text: And redundancy is really the entire point of this system.
segments.viText: Và sự dư thừa thực sự là toàn bộ quan điểm của hệ thống này.

segments.text: America doesn't simply have one command center.
segments.viText: Nước Mỹ không chỉ có một trung tâm chỉ huy.

segments.text: It has multiple command centers.
segments.viText: Nó có nhiều trung tâm chỉ huy.

segments.text: It doesn't have one communication system.
segments.viText: Nó không có một hệ thống liên lạc.

segments.text: It has multiple communication systems.
segments.viText: Nó có nhiều hệ thống thông tin liên lạc.

segments.text: And it doesn't rely entirely on aircraft sitting safely on the ground.
segments.viText: Và nó không hoàn toàn dựa vào việc máy bay đậu an toàn trên mặt đất.

segments.text: It has aircraft capable of taking those functions into the sky.
segments.viText: Nó có máy bay có khả năng thực hiện những chức năng đó trên bầu trời.

segments.text: Because the entire system is designed around one terrifying assumption.
segments.viText: Bởi vì toàn bộ hệ thống được thiết kế xoay quanh một giả định đáng sợ.

segments.text: What if everything else fails?
segments.viText: Điều gì sẽ xảy ra nếu mọi thứ khác đều thất bại?

segments.text: The E4B isn't designed to fly into a nuclear blast and simply emerge untouched.
segments.viText: E4B không được thiết kế để bay vào một vụ nổ hạt nhân và thoát ra mà không bị chạm tới.

segments.text: Instead, it is designed around something much more important.
segments.viText: Thay vào đó, nó được thiết kế xoay quanh một điều gì đó quan trọng hơn nhiều.

segments.text: Survival of command.
segments.viText: Sự sống sót của lệnh.

segments.text: The United States's nuclear arsenal only acts as a deterrent if an enemy believes
segments.viText: Kho vũ khí hạt nhân của Hoa Kỳ chỉ đóng vai trò răn đe nếu kẻ thù tin tưởng

segments.text: America can respond to an attack.
segments.viText: Mỹ có thể đáp trả một cuộc tấn công.

segments.text: Destroying Washington shouldn't mean destroying the country's ability to retaliate.
segments.viText: Tiêu diệt Washington không có nghĩa là tiêu diệt khả năng trả đũa của nước này.

segments.text: Destroying communication networks shouldn't mean losing contact with submarines.
segments.viText: Phá hủy mạng lưới liên lạc không có nghĩa là mất liên lạc với tàu ngầm.

segments.text: And destroying military command centers shouldn't mean there is nobody left to make decisions.
segments.viText: Và việc phá hủy các trung tâm chỉ huy quân sự không có nghĩa là không còn ai để đưa ra quyết định.

segments.text: That's what the doomsday plane is ultimately designed to prevent.
segments.viText: Đó chính là điều mà chiếc máy bay ngày tận thế cuối cùng được thiết kế để ngăn chặn.

segments.text: It turns one of the most vulnerable parts of nuclear warfare, the command structure,
segments.viText: Nó biến một trong những phần dễ bị tổn thương nhất của chiến tranh hạt nhân, cơ cấu chỉ huy,

segments.text: into something that can move.
segments.viText: vào một cái gì đó có thể di chuyển.

segments.text: A command center that can't be easily targeted because it is thousands of feet
segments.viText: Một trung tâm chỉ huy không thể dễ dàng bị nhắm mục tiêu vì nó cách xa hàng nghìn feet

segments.text: in the air.
segments.viText: trong không khí.

segments.text: A communication system that can use satellites, radio networks, and even a 5m long
segments.viText: Một hệ thống thông tin liên lạc có thể sử dụng vệ tinh, mạng vô tuyến và thậm chí cả đường truyền dài 5m

segments.text: trailing antenna.
segments.viText: anten kéo dài.

segments.text: And a military headquarters that can remain airborne for days if necessary.
segments.viText: Và một trụ sở quân sự có thể duy trì trên không trong nhiều ngày nếu cần thiết.

segments.text: It's an aircraft built around a concept that sounds almost contradictory.
segments.viText: Đó là một chiếc máy bay được chế tạo dựa trên một ý tưởng nghe có vẻ gần như trái ngược nhau.

segments.text: The less likely you think nuclear war is, the more useful the doomsday plane
segments.viText: Bạn càng ít nghĩ chiến tranh hạt nhân thì máy bay ngày tận thế càng hữu ích

segments.text: becomes because its existence is intended to make nuclear war less likely in the
segments.viText: trở nên như vậy bởi vì sự tồn tại của nó nhằm mục đích làm cho chiến tranh hạt nhân ít xảy ra hơn trong

segments.text: first place.
segments.viText: vị trí đầu tiên

segments.text: An enemy needs to believe that even a devastating first strike won't eliminate America's
segments.viText: Kẻ thù cần phải tin rằng ngay cả một đòn tấn công đầu tiên mang tính hủy diệt cũng sẽ không loại bỏ được

segments.text: ability to respond.
segments.viText: của Mỹ. khả năng đáp ứng.

segments.text: And as long as that belief exists, the doomsday plane doesn't need to do
segments.viText: Và chỉ cần niềm tin đó còn tồn tại thì máy bay ngày tận thế không cần phải làm

segments.text: what it was built for.
segments.viText: nó được xây dựng để làm gì.

segments.text: It simply needs to be ready.
segments.viText: Nó chỉ cần phải sẵn sàng.
